subtopicTitle: Converting between DCM, quaternions, Euler angles

cards.front: Define the Direction Cosine Matrix (DCM) $C$ for two right-handed frames.
cards.back: $C_{ij} = \mathbf{e}_i \cdot \mathbf{E}_j$, where $\mathbf{e}_i$ are unit vectors of the rotated frame and $\mathbf{E}_j$ of the reference frame. $C$ is orthogonal with $\det(C)=+1$.

cards.front: State the unit-norm constraint on a rotation quaternion $q = [q_0,\,\mathbf{q}]$.
cards.back: $q_0^2 + q_1^2 + q_2^2 + q_3^2 = 1$. This follows directly from the fact that rotation preserves vector length.

cards.front: Write the 3-2-1 Euler-angle sequence rotation matrix $C_{321}(\psi,\theta,\phi)$.
cards.back: $$C_{321}=\begin{bmatrix}c\theta c\psi & c\theta s\psi & -s\theta\\ s\phi s\theta c\psi-c\phi s\psi & s\phi s\theta s\psi+c\phi c\psi & s\phi c\theta\\ c\phi s\theta c\psi+s\phi s\psi & c\phi s\theta s\psi-s\phi c\psi & c\phi c\theta\end{bmatrix}$$

cards.front: Give the direct formula converting unit quaternion $q$ to DCM $C$.
Extract the 3-2-1 Euler angles from a given DCM $C$.
Convert 3-2-1 Euler angles $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$ to unit quaternion $q$.
Extract a unit quaternion from DCM $C$ using Shepperd’s method; include sign choice.
cards.back: Compute trace $t=\operatorname{tr}(C)$. Choose largest diagonal or off-diagonal; e.g. if $t>0$, $q_0=\frac12\sqrt{1+t}$, then $q_i=\frac14 q_0^{-1}(C_{jk}-C_{kj})$ (cyclic). Flip sign of $q$ if $q_0<0$ for continuity.

cards.front: Why do quaternions avoid gimbal lock while Euler angles do not?
cards.back: Euler angles parameterize SO(3) with three sequential rotations about moving axes, producing a coordinate singularity when two axes align. Quaternions embed SO(3) in the 3-sphere $S^3$ (double cover), a manifold without singularities.
